newsitem.title: POLAND: Rolimpex to buy sugar, fats producers.
newsitem.headline: Rolimpex to buy sugar, fats producers.

text.p: Polish food trader Rolimpex SA seeks to buy producers in the sugar and fats industries and gain 10- to 15-percent market shares there, the firm's spokesman said on Thursday.
"It's hard to say precisely that for example in 1997 we're going to buy four sugar plants...that give us 15 percent of the market, but our plans are in that direction," Bohdan Gornicki told Reuters.
He said Rolimpex already had about a 10-percent market share in producing fodder, seed and cereal products.
Gornicki said Rolimpex would try to get as many shares as possible in this month's public offering of 1.65 million shares in edible-fats producer Kruszwica SA.
The minimum price is 25 zlotys and investors will be able to register up to 10,000 shares from December 9-20.
Gornicki said Rolimpex was also considering buying fats makers Gdanskie Zaklady Tluszczowe and Zaklady Tluszczowe w Szamotulach (Szamotuly).

Rolimpex President Roman Mlyniec has earlier told Gazeta Wyborcza daily that the food trader was also considering buying sugar producers in the towns of Glinojeck, Ketrzyn and Ropczyce in its attempts to increase production activities.
In September Rolimpex bought sugar refinery Cukrownia Dobre w Dobrem Kujawskim (Dobre).

The company plans to use some of the $20 million the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said it would engage in Rolimpex after the bank bought a 10-percent stake in the food trader in July.
